Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has rewarded Nigeria’s victorious Flamingos with N10m each, alongside other gifts, following their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Sanwo-Olu announced the rewards on Sunday when he received the 21 players and nine members of the coaching crew and backroom staff, celebrating their achievement and urging them to remain focused on reaching greater heights in their careers. In addition to the cash gifts, each of the 21 players received an iPhone and a pair of headphones, which will be customised with their names. The Flamingos made history with their impressive campaign in Morocco, culminating in a victory over Japan in the final to claim the world title and becoming the first African team to achieve that. Addressing the players, the governor reminded them that winning the World Cup was only the beginning of their football careers, urging them to maintain the discipline and consistency required to reach the highest level. To get to the top might not be so difficult, but to sustain that pace, you need consistency,” Sanwo-Olu said. Flamingos captain Harmony Chidi, speaking on behalf of her teammates and the technical crew, thanked the governor for the gesture and pledged that the team would continue to make the country proud. “On behalf of my teammates and the technical crew, we want to appreciate you for your kindness. We promise you that we will keep making Nigerians proud,” she said. The Flamingos defeated Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat on November 7, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing Nigeria’s maiden title in the competition. Japan pulled one back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Nigerian youngsters held on to become the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.
